{{Short description|None}}
{{Use Canadian English|date=January 2023}}
Below is a list of the [[Premier of Ontario|premiers]] of the province of [[Ontario]], Canada, since [[Canadian Confederation|Confederation]] in 1867. Ontario uses a unicameral [[Westminster System|Westminster-style]] [[parliamentary government]], in which the premier is the leader of the party that controls the most seats in the [[Legislative Assembly of Ontario|Legislative Assembly]]. The premier is Ontario's [[head of government]]. The premier picks a cabinet from the elected members to form the [[Executive Council of Ontario]], and presides over that body.

Members are first elected to the legislature during [[List of Ontario general elections|general elections]]. General elections must be conducted every four years from the date of the last election. An election may also happen if the Governing party loses the confidence of the legislature, by the defeat of a supply bill or tabling of a confidence motion.

This article only covers the time since the [[Canadian Confederation]] was created in 1867. For the premiers of [[Canada West]] from 1840 to 1867, see [[List of joint premiers of the Province of Canada]].

The 26th and current premier of Ontario is [[Doug Ford]] of the [[Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario]] since June 29, 2018.

==Premiers of Ontario since 1867==

|accomplishments = Prior to Confederation in 1867, Sandfield Macdonald was a genuine Liberal/Reform Party Member of the Legislative Assembly of the Province of Canada and a rival of Sir John A Macdonald. He led a Liberal ministry between 1862 and 1864, the only significant interruption of [[John A. Macdonald|John A Macdonald]]'s rule in the final decade of the united province. Despite being an opponent confederation, Sanfield Macdonald accepted Sir John A's offer of the permiership upon the founding of Canada, and led a notional [[coalition government|Coalition]] (the "[[Patent Combination]]") supported by the [[Conservative Party of Ontario|Conservative Party]] and only a handful of [[Ontario Liberal Party|Liberal]] members. He was simultaneously an MP in the House of Commons until 1872.
|tenure          = {{Age in years and days|1867|07|15|1871|12|20}}
